subject: general
question: A bus travelling at 84 km/hr completes a journey in 20 hours. What should its speed be to cover the same distance in 10 hours?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When distance is constant, Speed is inversely proportional to Time.

Time ratio = T₁ : T₂ = 20 : 10 = 2 : 1

Speed ratio = S₁ : S₂ = 1 : 2

Given S₁ (1 unit) = 84 km/hr

New speed S₂ (2 units) = 84 × 2 = 168 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 168 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial speed (S₁) = 84 km/hr

Initial time (T₁) = 20 hours

New time (T₂) = 10 hours

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

 
• 
 
 
 

 Distance (D) is Constant
 
 Time = 20 hours
 Speed = 84 km/hr
 
 Time = 10 hours
 Speed = ?

**Calculation:**

⇒ Distance covered = 84 × 20

⇒ Distance = 1680 km

⇒ Now, the same distance is to be covered in 10 hours.

⇒ New Speed = Distance ÷ New Time

⇒ New Speed = 1680 ÷ 10

⇒ New Speed = 168 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 168 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed

Average speed is the total distance traveled divided by the total time taken. If a distance is covered at speed x and the same distance is returned at speed y, Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Relative Speed

For two objects moving in the same direction, relative speed is the difference of their speeds (S₁ − S₂). For opposite directions, it is the sum of their speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Proportionality in Time & Distance

If Distance is constant, Speed ∝ 1 ÷ Time. If Time is constant, Distance ∝ Speed. If Speed is constant, Distance ∝ Time.
